correctness.rationale: Under lambda4*mu4*tau nonzero, the cited construction is in the normal multiplicative branch. The source reduces the relevant Mordell-Weil section count to common roots alpha of two displayed equations and proves sigma=3-m when there are 2^m common roots. The case (lambda2,mu2)=(0,0) gives exactly four roots. Otherwise any nonzero root is uniquely alpha=mu2/lambda2, and direct substitution is equivalent to Delta=0; this gives exactly two roots on Delta=0 and one root off it. The symbolic verifier checks the only nontrivial elimination identity. The proof explicitly separates these algebraic facts from the source-supplied lattice formula.

value.rationale: The Artin invariant is the central discrete invariant classifying supersingular K3 Picard lattices. The source establishes only the range 1<=sigma<=3 and existence of all values; locating the jumps exactly turns that qualitative statement into a usable parameter stratification. The cubic equation shows where the Picard discriminant changes, the origin explains the deeper jump, and the fixed-leading-coefficient slice reveals three natural sigma=2 branches. This is a motivated structural refinement rather than an arbitrary specialization or a recomputation of a known table.
